meta.status: accepted design refined by #145; not in force until #140
meta.description: Separates candidate assertions, language-bearing card releases, and positively evidenced manufactured printings. The dry run maps every legacy/source input onto this boundary without changing an authoritative store.
meta.notAnEvidenceChange: Authority tiers, providerId, corroboration, absence scopes and owner adjudications are untouched. This schema controls when an assertion may create an existence-bearing node; #137 controls evidence inference.

candidate_claim.grain: one assertion from one legacy or source record about a proposed card release or physical printing

dispositions.established-and-mapped: positive evidence permits the proposed target to exist
dispositions.candidate-needs-evidence: the assertion remains visible but cannot create a target
dispositions.bounded-contradicted: preserves an existing contradicted verdict as a non-materializing claim; #137 governs any future inference
dispositions.positively-excluded: the source record is outside the physical-card product scope for a stated reason

candidate_claim.note: A candidate claim is not a weak entity. It is the durable record that a question was asked, including contradicted and marketplace-only inputs.

work.grain: one shared card text/artwork identity independent of a local release
work.note: The legacy cardKey groups name plus attacks and does not prove artwork equivalence. Source-first records may leave the work edge unresolved.

set_edition.grain: one local set/product edition with one explicit locality and printed-language/script profile

states.identified: the local set code is positively identified
states.needs-local-identifier: a card release establishes that an edition exists but its local code is not recorded

set_edition.note: This is the minimum identity boundary required by #145. #146 adds set concepts, release events, market waves and complete catalogue semantics.

card_release.grain: one card-number slot in one set edition, before finish/stamp/error manufacturing distinctions

states.identified: local set code and collector number are known
states.needs-local-identifier: positive evidence establishes the localized release but its own local identifiers are not recorded

card_release.note: Variant tokens do not belong in this identity. Several positively evidenced finishes or Cardmarket variants may realize one language-bearing card release.

physical_printing.grain: one positively evidenced manufactured finish/treatment/distribution/error realization of a card release
physical_printing.note: A language confirmation alone establishes at most a card release. A physical-printing node requires positive evidence for the manufactured classification.

language.note: Language is part of set-edition identity. Spanish spans WEST and LATAM; English spans WEST and SEA.

source_record.grain: one immutable legacy, provider, specimen, or finish record
source_record.note: Existing evidence ids and provider records remain the inputs of record.

evidence_observation.grain: one immutable positive observation or contradiction supported by a named bounded-exhaustive surface
evidence_observation.note: This model does not re-adjudicate observations. Existing unit, specimen and finish evidence back-projects unchanged; #137 owns evidence inference.

alias_or_equivalence_assertion.grain: one provenance-bearing relationship between a raw identifier and a graph node, or between two graph nodes

candidate_claim--materializes-->target.guard: only a permitted positive evidenceStatus may populate materializedTargetId

card_release--implements-->work.note: zero is an explicit needs-equivalence state, never a guessed edge

I1.rule: language is not locality, and both are explicit on a set edition
I1.detail: No consumer derives either dimension from the other.

I2.rule: a contradicted, unresolved, excluded, or marketplace-only claim cannot mint an existence-bearing target

I3.rule: one card release belongs to exactly one language-bearing set edition
I3.detail: BKT 118 in seven confirmed languages is seven card releases, not one WEST print with a languages array.

I4.rule: manufacturing classifications specialize a card release rather than changing its set identity
I4.detail: Finish, pattern, stamp, size, distribution and explicit error class live on physical_printing.

I5.rule: card releases sharing a work remain distinct releases
I5.detail: Japanese sm10 076 and Traditional-Chinese AS5a 142 may share a work edge and are different card releases.

I6.rule: aliases and equivalence proposals never erase raw identifiers and never merge automatically

I7.rule: an error printing requires positive evidence plus an explicit error classification
I7.detail: A finish or variant pass cannot mint an error node as a side effect.

I8.rule: localSetCode and localNumber are null exactly when localIdentifierKnown is false
I8.detail: Migration anchors remain in viaLegacy fields and cannot masquerade as local identifiers.

I9.rule: release dates and set availability are context only and cannot establish a card release
I9.detail: Existence-bearing nodes require a permitted evidence observation; temporal catalogue metadata is never a promotion trigger.

futureDatabaseConstraints: candidate_claim.materializedTargetId is null unless disposition is established-and-mapped
card_release.setEditionId is a required foreign key
card_release has exactly one non-empty language and script through its set edition
card_release local identifiers are both null or both identified according to localIdentifierKnown
physical_printing.cardReleaseId and establishingClaimId are required foreign keys
physical_printing establishing claim has permitted positive evidence
errorClass is null unless an explicit error-classification assertion exists
raw aliases and migration anchors are retained under uniqueness constraints

dispositions.carried: one legacy product maps to one established release
dispositions.split: one legacy product maps to several language-bearing releases
dispositions.established-and-mapped: a positive claim maps to an established target
dispositions.candidate-needs-evidence: a claim remains visible without creating a target
dispositions.bounded-contradicted: an existing contradicted verdict remains visible and cannot create a target; #137 owns future inference
dispositions.positively-excluded: an input is outside physical-card scope for a stated reason

rules: Every legacy/source input carries exactly one disposition.
A back-projection reproduces the legacy/source identifiers and statuses.
Existing verdicts and evidence migrate as recorded and are never re-derived here.
No absence or marketplace hint creates an existence-bearing node.
Migration anchors are replaceable by explicit aliases when local identifiers are discovered.

acceptanceFixtures.tests: all underlying contradicted claims remain candidates and create no card release
one confirmed and one contradicted variant share a release without transferring status
source-first local releases have their own edition/release identity

ownerDecisions.D1: Every catch-up code backed by a physical specimen enters as a local release; raw source_first_prints printId values remain aliases until #140.
ownerDecisions.D2: Established releases with unknown local identifiers remain visible as needs-local-identifier.
ownerDecisions.D3: European Spanish and LATAM Spanish are distinct localities of one language and both are in scope.
ownerDecisions.D4: A positively evidenced and explicitly classified error is its own physical-printing node.
